bib.title: StarCoder: may the source be with you!

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Appendix A regexes, Table B.1 country list and the per-language rows of Tables 1-3 not transcribed.

question: Can an open-access, permissively-licensed-data, responsibly released 15.5B code LLM match or beat existing open and closed code models across languages and tasks?
contributions: Release StarCoderBase and StarCoder, open-access 15.5B Code LLMs trained on 80+ languages with 8K context, FIM and multi-query attention
Most comprehensive evaluation of Code LLMs to date: StarCoder beats every open multi-language code LLM, matches or beats code-cushman-001, and beats Python-fine-tuned models when fine-tuned on Python

Safer release: OpenRAIL-M licence, attribution tracing tool (Bloom-filter membership check plus BM25 index), improved PII redaction with a 12,000-file / 22,950-entity annotated dataset and StarEncoder

method.summary: StarCoderBase (15.5B decoder-only, MQA, FIM, 8K context) is pretrained for 1T tokens on a filtered, near-deduplicated, PII-redacted 86-language subset of The Stack v1.2 plus GitHub issues, Git commits and Jupyter notebooks. StarCoder is StarCoderBase fine-tuned for about 2 epochs (35B tokens) on the Python subset. Both are evaluated on code (HumanEval, MBPP, DS-1000, ODEX, MultiPL-E, FIM, type prediction, docstrings, security) and natural-language benchmarks.
method.task: next-token pretraining with fill-in-the-middle on source code, issues, commits and notebooks

datasets.name: The Stack v1.2 subset (86 languages, plus issues, commits, notebooks)
datasets.size: Table 1/2 total: 305,929,658 files, 815.68 GB after dedup, 799.37 GB after filters and decontamination; ~1T training tokens
datasets.split: sampled proportionally to volume (natural distribution); JSON and YAML reweighted to 1 GB each, CSS to 3 GB; Python 60.40 GB = 7.875%
datasets.source: The Stack v1.2 (Kocetkov et al., 2022): permissively licensed GitHub repositories, 44 opt-outs at processing time; Git commits from BigQuery
datasets.preprocessing: 86 of 358 languages kept (>500 MB or top-50 Githut 2.0 / Dec 2022 TIOBE, plus dialects); visual inspection of up to 1,000 files per extension, 18 annotators, 300 extensions, 36 extensions dropped, long-line filter removed for 27; XML filter ('<?xml version=' in first 100 chars); alpha filter (<25% alphabetic removed, checked on top 25 extensions); HTML visible-text >=20% and >=100 chars; YAML 50-5000 chars, avg line <100, max line <1000, >50% alphabetic (removes ~20% files, 90% volume); JSON 50-5000 chars, >50% alphabetic (removes ~70% files, 98% volume); MinHash + LSH near-dedup with 5-grams and Jaccard 0.7 (not applied to Git commits or issues); decontamination removes files with HumanEval/MBPP docstrings or solutions, APPS docstrings, GSM8K questions, DS-1000 prompts (Python worst: 558 files removed); PII redaction

datasets.name: GitHub issues
datasets.preprocessing: strip email-reply boilerplate, drop messages <200 chars, truncate long comments to 100 lines keeping last 20 (18% of volume removed); drop bot comments (17% of events, 14.7% of issues emptied); keep >=2 users or single-user with <7,000 chars, drop single-user issues with >10 events (14% more removed); fasttext English filter; usernames replaced by participant counters

datasets.name: Git commits
datasets.size: raw ~4 TB; 7,674,345 commits, 64 GB (32.00 GB weight, 4.172%)
datasets.source: BigQuery single-file commits, same licences and extensions as The Stack, opted-out users removed
datasets.preprocessing: Table 4 filters (>100k chars removed, <=2-line changes kept at 50%, >=200-line changes kept at 10%, empty subjects, bot-like messages, hash messages, data formats 50%); full file used 20% of time, otherwise a window of 0-32 lines around first and last changed line; not near-deduplicated

datasets.name: Jupyter scripts
datasets.preprocessing: Jupytext conversion; language from metadata, Guesslang (probability >=0.5) cut unidentified notebooks to 6,400 from >30,000

datasets.name: Jupyter structured
datasets.preprocessing: consecutive markdown/code blocks merged into text-code-output chains; <empty_output> token for empty outputs; only last output kept when blocks merged

datasets.name: Annotated PII dataset
datasets.size: 12,000 files (~50 lines each, 31 languages), 22,950 entities; train 7,878 / test 4,000 examples
datasets.split: 7,878 train, 4,000 test, balanced across PII types
datasets.source: Toloka crowd-workers (1,399 from 35 countries, $7.30/h); 7,100 files pre-filtered with detect-secrets and regexes, 5,100 random
datasets.preprocessing: IDs excluded for low annotation quality; plus 400 annotated files from Ben Allal et al. (2023) and 18,000 pseudo-labelled files

models.name: StarCoderBase
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer, multi-query attention, learned absolute positional embeddings, FlashAttention, same as SantaCoder
models.tokenizer: byte-level BPE (HF Tokenizers), digit-splitter plus GPT-2 regex pre-tokenizer

other.training: 100,000 steps, global batch 4,096 sequences of max length 1,024, ~400B tokens, ~2 days on 64 A100

models.name: SantaCoder
models.architecture: MQA decoder; 24 layers, hidden 2048, 16 heads, 2048 positions

models.name: CodeGen-16B-Multi / Mono, CodeGeeX-13B, code-cushman-001, code-davinci-001/002, InCoder-6B, LLaMA 7B-65B, PaLM, LaMDA, GPT-NeoX-20B, others

training.objective: causal LM with fill-in-the-middle on code (FIM rate 0.5, PSM/SPMv2 each 0.5, character level); StarEncoder: MLM+NSP
training.precision: BF16 (10% lower throughput than FP16, chosen to avoid instabilities)
training.hardware: 512 A100 80GB GPUs on 64 nodes; 3D parallel: tensor and pipeline parallel rank 4 (16 GPUs per replica), 32-way data parallel, micro-batch 1, 16 accumulation steps, Megatron-LM distributed optimizer
training.compute: 320,256 GPU hours (StarCoderBase), 280 W per GPU, 89,671.68 kWh, 16.68 tCO2eq; fine-tune adds 3.5% time, 0.58 tCO2eq

other.metadata_prefix: <reponame>, <filename>, <gh_stars> (buckets 0, 1-10, 10-100, 100-1000, 1000+), each prefixed independently at random with probability 0.2
other.few_restarts: except for a few restarts, no significant instabilities
other.natural_language_share: Roughly 20% of training tokens: 7% GitHub issues, 10% Markdown, 2% Jupyter notebooks, 4% HTML (as printed; components sum to 23%)

inference.decoding: sampling; greedy for return type prediction, docstring generation, GSM8K greedy; nucleus p=0.95 temp 0.7 for majority vote; nucleus p=0.95 for toxicity
inference.temperature: 0.2 for pass@1, 0.8 for k>1 (HumanEval/MBPP/MultiPL-E); 0.2 for DS-1000 and Asleep at the Keyboard; 0.1 for the E.3 prompt
inference.top_p: 0.5 for DS-1000; 0.95 for toxicity and maj@k
inference.samples: n=200 per problem for open-access models (HumanEval/MBPP/MultiPL-E), n=20 for API models; DS-1000 mean pass@1 over 40 samples; Asleep at the Keyboard 25 completions per scenario (1,000 per model); ODEX n not stated
inference.prompting: GSM8K 8-shot CoT and PAL; MMLU 5-shot; CoQA zero-shot; docstring generation zero-shot via infilling; technical-assistant HHH-style prompt (Appendix F)

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: fraction of problems for which any of k samples passes all tests (Chen et al., 2021)

metrics.name: Insecure rate (Asleep at the Keyboard)
metrics.definition: fraction of syntactically valid completions containing the tested vulnerability

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: return type prediction on normalized annotations

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: smoothed 4-gram BLEU on first line of docstring

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: on last 1K tokens of 8K chunks with 2K vs 8K window, 10 GPL repos per language

metrics.name: Toxicity
metrics.definition: percentage of 10K RealToxicityPrompts responses flagged by RoBERTa classifier (threshold 0.5) or offensive word list

eval.protocol: Code LM Evaluation Harness (docker execution, data parallel); single runs; no significance tests reported; model checkpoints at every 200B tokens evaluated in 6.3.

availability.code: open-sourced code repositories on GitHub (bigcode-project) and evaluation harness
availability.weights: public under OpenRAIL-M licence (more commercially viable version)
availability.data: The Stack public; PII annotations gated; training and eval splits gated access at hf.co/BigCode

limits: Licence detector may misclassify repositories; opt-out works per repository and cannot remove duplicates elsewhere.
PII detector has false positives and negatives; usernames excluded from redaction because of low performance; model may still emit PII.
The Stack may contain undetected malicious code; 654 files flagged and removed.
Attribution tools (Bloom filter, BM25) cover only the training subset, may give false positives and do not separate generic from protected code.
Return-type and docstring benchmarks may overlap with training data.
Near-deduplication not applied to Git commits or issues (time constraints); Swift and D omitted from training languages (Swift by human error).
StarCoder surprisingly beats StarCoderBase on some non-Python languages and authors can only speculate why.
Training token share of natural language stated as roughly 20% but listed components sum to 23%.
No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; single training run.
